clue.text: Extravagantly update car, finally, and exchange Ford for Ferrari, perhaps

indicators.note: done extravagantly, with wild flourish, so the letters of the words before are thrown into a new order
finally points to the closing letter of the word car

explanation.surface: A spendthrift motorist decides to splash out, swapping a humble Ford for a Ferrari.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extravagantly' shuffles UPDATE together with R, the last letter of 'car' picked out by 'finally'.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap something modest for a costlier, better model is the phrasal verb meaning upgrade; the Ferrari is just an example.

clue.text: Animal on the loose in gorge

parts.note: a pig is a farm animal
an escaped creature is out, roaming free

explanation.surface: An escaped beast is running wild through a narrow ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' looks like a canyon where the animal roams, but it is the verb: to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to stuff oneself with food, a phrasal verb synonym of the verb sense of gorge.

clue.text: Fruit and vegetable recipe

parts.note: a pea is a green vegetable
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on old prescriptions

explanation.surface: A shopping list item: some fruit and a vegetable dish to cook.
explanation.walkthrough: R for 'recipe' comes from the Latin 'recipe' (take) heading prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: The juicy, tapering orchard produce of a tree is a classic example of a fruit.

clue.text: Suppose a drunk makes liquid lunches?

indicators.note: something drunk staggers about, so the letters of the words before it are reeled into a new order

explanation.surface: Speculating that a tippler's midday meal is really just beer.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'liquid lunch' normally means alcohol; here it is soup, which is literally liquid, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick soups made from dried split legumes are a meal you eat by the spoonful, so playfully a lunch that is liquid.

clue.text: Athletes retreating two steps at the start? They make us groan

indicators.text: retreating two steps at the start
indicators.note: the opening letter steps back two places in the alphabet, R going back through Q to the letter before it

parts.note: runners are track athletes

explanation.surface: Sprinters are penalised two paces at the starting line, and the crowd groans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating two steps at the start' moves the first letter R back two places in the alphabet (R, Q, P), fitting the Ps and Qs theme.
explanation.definitionFit: People who make bad wordplay jokes are notorious for drawing groans from listeners.

clue.text: Work discussing ten square chains becomes more baffling

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: discussing is talking about, so the letters are what is said out loud, not what is written

parts.note: ten square chains make one acre, the old unit of land area

explanation.surface: A treatise on obscure land-measure conversions grows ever more confusing.
explanation.walkthrough: A chain is an old 22-yard length; ten square chains make an acre. 'discussing' signals the word is spoken, not spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque in its figurative sense means hard to understand, so the comparative is harder still to grasp.

clue.text: Unconventional requital for one fourth of the population

indicators.note: unconventional means out of the usual order, so the letters of requital are reorganised

explanation.surface: An unusual form of payback is handed out to a quarter of all people.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics, each of the four equal divisions of a ranked population is called this.

clue.text: A French electronic device gets minimal support

parts.note: un is the French for a
an iPod is Apple's portable music player

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's gadget is barely holding up.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-legged stand for a camera is the barest possible prop, fewer legs than a tripod.

clue.text: Provides jokes on the internet?

parts.note: E as in e-mail marks something online
quips are witty remarks

explanation.surface: A website that supplies gags online.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish someone with what they need is a direct synonym of supplying them.

clue.text: Pay attention: genius solver's getting theme

parts.note: a great mind is a genius
the solver is you, so the solver's is your
the puzzle's theme is the letters P and Q, filling many answers

explanation.surface: A setter flatters the clever solver: listen, here comes the theme.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is literal: answers throughout are packed with Ps and Qs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells someone to be careful about their manners and behaviour, to take care.

clue.text: Flirt with Romeo, leaving game

indicators.note: Romeo leaving means that letter departs from the game's name

parts.note: croquet is the lawn game with mallets and hoops
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone toys with a Romeo before walking out of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word, used as a verb, for trifling amorously or playing the coquette.

clue.text: Animal's hide when given away

definitions.meaning: with away added, the phrasal verb means to stash or hoard something

explanation.surface: An animal's pelt is handed over as a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like the animal's skin; it is the verb to conceal, which becomes the answer once 'away' is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The rodent famously stores nuts, giving the phrasal verb for hoarding things out of sight.

clue.text: Jet's prompt, ahead of time

indicators.note: the first piece stands in front of the next one

parts.note: to spur is to urge on

explanation.surface: An aircraft is told to leave early.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden gush of liquid is a jet, as from a hose.

clue.text: Remain and hunt for what's left

parts.note: to be is to remain or exist
a quest is a search

explanation.surface: Stay put and search for the leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's left' looks like leftovers but means what is left in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy handed down in a will is what a dead person has left to someone.

clue.text: Spat out everything, but sent back taro, as predicted

indicators.note: but in the sense of except: everything except a certain run of letters

parts.note: to expectorate is to cough up and spit

indicators.note: sent back means the word taro is read backwards

explanation.surface: A diner spits out everything except the taro, which goes back to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns TARO into ORAT; 'but' (except) removes that run from EXPECTORATED.
explanation.definitionFit: What was foreseen or anticipated in advance is a direct synonym of what was predicted.

clue.text: Wait ended after Queen rejected continental alliance twice

indicators.note: the last piece comes after the rest
rejected means the letters are turned back, read in reverse
twice means the alliance's letters are written two times over

parts.note: the EU is the European Union
time is up when it has ended

explanation.surface: A monarch snubs a European bloc twice over, and the long hold-up is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles EU to EUEU; 'rejected' reverses that to UEUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand in line for one's turn is the very British way to wait.

clue.text: Pence dispatched again and put on display

parts.note: something resent is sent once more

explanation.surface: The coins went out a second time and were exhibited.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something publicly, as in a gallery or on stage, is to exhibit it.

clue.text: Man on board meets strange (naked) old adventurer

parts.note: a chessman: P stands for pawn in chess notation

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: bizarre means strange

explanation.surface: A sailor encounters a bizarre unclothed figure from history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' looks like a sailor but is a chess piece. 'naked' strips BIZARRE to IZARR.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Pizarro was the sixteenth-century Spanish conquistador who conquered the Inca empire.

clue.text: India's ready and preposterously sure about exercise

indicators.note: about means going round, so the scrambled letters surround the exercise
preposterously means absurdly, so the letters of sure are put in a nonsensical order

parts.note: PE is physical education

explanation.surface: India is prepared and absurdly confident about its training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preposterously' gives RUES; 'about' wraps it round the exercise. 'Ready' is British slang for cash ('the readies').
explanation.definitionFit: The currency units of India are its money, and ready is slang for cash.

clue.text: Without hesitation, shelter Mary Jane in vessel

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the hesitation is taken out

parts.note: to quarter is to lodge or house
er is a sound of hesitation
Mary Jane is slang for marijuana, also called pot

explanation.surface: Decisively, someone stashes cannabis inside a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking mug holding two pints is a container, so a type of vessel.

clue.text: Set clue needing a measure of intelligence to penetrate

indicators.note: penetrate means to pierce, so the measure goes inside the word clue

parts.note: IQ, intelligence quotient

explanation.surface: A cryptic clue has been set that needs real brainpower to crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a verb about setting a clue, but it is the noun: a group.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclusive circle of people is a set or coterie.

clue.text: Be brave, I punch erratically

indicators.note: erratically means irregularly, so the letters of the words before are put in a random order

explanation.surface: A boxer urges courage while throwing wild punches.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhortation to keep cheerful and courageous in adversity.

clue.text: A diva's quite confused about group of followers, though seemingly sophisticated

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the group
confused means muddled, so the letters of the words before are jumbled

parts.note: a cult is a devoted band of followers

explanation.surface: A prima donna is bemused by her fan club, who only appear refined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' jumbles the eleven letters of 'A diva's quite'; 'about' wraps them round the group of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: Quasi- means apparently or in part, so it describes refinement that is only on the surface.

clue.text: Addendum: I lied at first about how to get thin from gluttony, maybe

definitions.text: how to get thin from gluttony, maybe

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an addendum to a letter

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letters of the words I and lied

explanation.surface: A postscript confesses to lying about a weight-loss trick for overeaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes I and L; 'about' reverses PS + IL. Gluttony is a sin, and someone with this speech defect says 'sin' as 'thin'.
explanation.definitionFit: This speech impediment turns an S into a TH sound, so sin becomes thin.

clue.text: One of five at the present time can afford fruit

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets
CE, Common Era, is the present era of dating

explanation.surface: One of quintuplets can now pay for some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard, golden, pear-shaped orchard produce used for jelly and preserves.

clue.text: HQ Russia built shaped approximately like a block

indicators.note: built means constructed, so the letters are assembled into a new form

explanation.surface: Russia built a headquarters that is roughly box-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish means roughly, so something roughly four-sided and boxy.
